hyps.why: Removing a strong conv on the direct input-to-output edge costs more than removing a weaker op.
Adding a conv where the final edge was absent restores a strong path to the output.
Replacing a skip with a conv on the first edge yields large gains compared with replacing other ops.
Upgrading a skip to a conv on the direct edge gives larger gains than other replacements.
Skip-heavy parents gain a lot from a conv on edge 4.
Adding a skip to a missing direct edge helps, while replacing a conv with a skip hurts.
Replacing pooling with a conv gives large gains.
Adding pooling to a missing edge in a skip-heavy cell was strongly harmful.
Removing a skip in an all-skip cell improved accuracy, unlike removing a conv.
Removing a skip in an all-skip cell improved accuracy, unlike removing a conv.
